claims.text: Compositionally complex or high-entropy alloy systems can be used to exhibit a ductile–brittle–ductile transition.
Compositionally complex or high-entropy alloys are resistant to temper embrittlement.
Resistance to temper embrittlement enables the proposed ductile–brittle–ductile transition.
Molecular-dynamics simulations of alloy deformation can reveal atomic-scale mechanisms relevant to the transition.
Temper embrittlement occurs in conventional alloys within a narrow temperature window.
Atomic-scale mechanisms govern the ductile–brittle–ductile transition.
Simulations of alloy deformation can predict optimal alloy compositions and temperatures.
The proposed alloys will display a ductile–brittle–ductile transition without significant loss of ductility.

contradictions.description: A ductile–brittle–ductile transition necessarily includes an intermediate brittle response, whereas the predicted outcome states that the transition occurs without significant loss of ductility.

Resistance to temper embrittlement is offered as the reason for producing a brittle intermediate state, but no distinct physical mechanism connecting that resistance to brittle behavior is supplied; the stated mechanism is instead a simulation/prediction procedure.
